/-!
# Conjecture 9.41

by P. M. Neumann

Let $\Omega$ be a countably infinite set. For $k \geq 2$ define a *$k$-section* of
$\Omega$ to be a partition of $\Omega$ as union of $k$ infinite sets.

b) Does there exist a group that is transitive on $k$-sections but not on
$(k + 1)$-sections?

Here a "group" is a permutation group $G \leq \mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$, acting on the set of
$k$-sections by moving the blocks of a partition: $g \cdot \{A_1, \ldots, A_k\} =
\{g(A_1), \ldots, g(A_k)\}$. "Transitive on $k$-sections" means that this induced action
on the set of all $k$-sections has a single orbit.

Part c) of the problem (a proper transitive subgroup of $\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$ transitive
on $\aleph_0$-sections) has a positive answer consistent with ZFC
(S. M. Corson, S. Shelah, [arXiv:2503.12997](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12997)) and is
not formalised here.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 9.41
- [S. M. Corson, S. Shelah, *A permutation group acting transitively on certain
  collections of models*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12997)
-/

def IsSection (k : ℕ) (P : Set (Set Ω)) : Prop :=
  Setoid.IsPartition P ∧ (∀ A ∈ P, A.Infinite) ∧ P.encard = k
blocks.docstring:
A `k`-section of `Ω`: a partition of `Ω` into exactly `k` infinite sets. A partition is
recorded as the (unordered) set `P` of its blocks; `P.encard = k` forces `P` to be finite
with exactly `k` blocks.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Setoid.IsPartition` (used as a component; it lacks the block-count and infinitude conditions), `Finpartition` (requires a lattice element / finite ambient structure and is unsuitable for infinite blocks of `Set Ω` indexed by a `Finset`), `Setoid Ω` with conditions on classes (would require a bespoke `MulAction (Equiv.Perm Ω) (Setoid Ω)`, which Mathlib lacks).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.41».IsSection
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of 'partition into exactly k infinite blocks'. Defined as `Setoid.IsPartition P ∧ (∀ A ∈ P, A.Infinite) ∧ P.encard = k` on `P : Set (Set Ω)`, so a section is an unordered set of blocks, exactly as in 'partition of Ω as union of k infinite sets'. `encard = k` forces finiteness with exactly k blocks (API lemma `IsSection.finite` included).

blocks.name: IsSection
blocks.text:
/-- A `k`-section of `Ω`: a partition of `Ω` into exactly `k` infinite sets. A partition is
recorded as the (unordered) set `P` of its blocks; `P.encard = k` forces `P` to be finite
with exactly `k` blocks. -/
def IsSection (k : ℕ) (P : Set (Set Ω)) : Prop :=

blocks.code:
def IsTransitiveOnSections (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ P Q : Set (Set Ω), IsSection k P → IsSection k Q → ∃ g ∈ G, g • P = Q
blocks.docstring:
A permutation group `G ≤ Sym(Ω)` is transitive on `k`-sections if for any two
`k`-sections `P` and `Q` there is some `g ∈ G` carrying `P` to `Q`. Here `g • P` is the
pointwise action `{g '' A | A ∈ P}` of `g` on the set of blocks of `P`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `MulAction.IsPretransitive G X` — would require constructing the induced `MulAction ↥G {P // IsSection k P}` instance; the direct ∀∃ formulation is equivalent (single orbit) and more transparent.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.41».IsTransitiveOnSections
justification.why_needed: Transitivity of a subgroup `G ≤ Sym(Ω)` on the set of k-sections: `∀ P Q, IsSection k P → IsSection k Q → ∃ g ∈ G, g • P = Q`, where `g • P` is Mathlib's pointwise action on `Set (Set Ω)` (verified by a `rfl` test to equal `(fun A => g '' A) '' P`). Stated directly rather than via `MulAction.IsPretransitive` on a subtype, which would need an extra `SubMulAction`/restricted-action instance and obscure the statement.

blocks.name: IsTransitiveOnSections
blocks.text:
/-- A permutation group `G ≤ Sym(Ω)` is transitive on `k`-sections if for any two
`k`-sections `P` and `Q` there is some `g ∈ G` carrying `P` to `Q`. Here `g • P` is the
pointwise action `{g '' A | A ∈ P}` of `g` on the set of blocks of `P`. -/
def IsTransitiveOnSections (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ P Q : Set (Set Ω), IsSection k P → IsSection k Q → ∃ g ∈ G, g • P = Q

theorem isSection_even_odd : IsSection 2 {{n : ℕ | Even n}, {n : ℕ | Odd n}} := by
  have hne : {n : ℕ | Even n} ≠ {n : ℕ | Odd n} := by
    intro h
    have : (0 : ℕ) ∈ {n : ℕ | Odd n} := h ▸ Even.zero
    simp at this
  refine ⟨⟨?_, fun a => ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, not_or]
    constructor
    · intro h
      have : (0 : ℕ) ∈ {n : ℕ | Even n} := Even.zero
      simp [← h] at this
    · intro h
      have : (1 : ℕ) ∈ {n : ℕ | Odd n} := odd_one
      simp [← h] at this
  · rcases Nat.even_or_odd a with ha | ha
    · refine ⟨{n : ℕ | Even n}, ⟨by simp, ha⟩, ?_⟩
      rintro b ⟨hb, hab⟩
      simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hb
      rcases hb with rfl | rfl
      · rfl
      · exact absurd ha (Nat.not_even_iff_odd.mpr hab)
    · refine ⟨{n : ℕ | Odd n}, ⟨by simp, ha⟩, ?_⟩
      rintro b ⟨hb, hab⟩
      simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hb
      rcases hb with rfl | rfl
      · exact absurd ha (Nat.not_odd_iff_even.mpr hab)
      · rfl
  · simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq_or_imp, forall_eq]
    constructor
    · exact Set.infinite_of_not_bddAbove fun ⟨M, hM⟩ =>
        absurd (hM (show Even (2 * (M + 1)) from even_two_mul _)) (by omega)
    · exact Set.infinite_of_not_bddAbove fun ⟨M, hM⟩ =>
        absurd (hM (show Odd (2 * M + 1) from odd_two_mul_add_one _)) (by omega)
  · rw [Set.encard_pair hne]
    rfl

claims.decomposer_note: Here 'group' means a permutation group G ≤ Sym(Ω) on the countably infinite set Ω acting on k-sections (unordered partitions of Ω into k infinite blocks, k ≥ 2 as fixed in the preamble); the quantifier on k is implicit and should be read as 'for every k ≥ 2 does there exist such a G' (with the (k+1)-section action referring to the same G), and 'transitive on k-sections' means the induced action on the set of all k-sections has a single orbit.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the slot with the same logical shape fixed by the decomposition table: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ countably infinite Ω, ∀ k ≥ 2, ∃ G ≤ Sym(Ω) transitive on (unordered) k-sections and not transitive on (k+1)-sections, same G in both conditions, no extra transitivity/properness hypotheses (those belong to part c). All compile. c07 was chosen as the base because its encoding is the cleanest and most robust: a k-section is a `Set (Set Ω)` that is a `Setoid.IsPartition` (nonempty, pairwise disjoint, covering blocks) with every block infinite and `encard = k` (exact block count, forces finiteness, avoids the ncard/Nat.card = 0-on-infinite convention used by c03/c08 and the ad-hoc Finite ∧ ncard of c02); transitivity is `∀ P Q sections, ∃ g ∈ G, g • P = Q` with the scoped Pointwise action, pinned down by a `rfl` test lemma to be the block-moving action {g '' A | A ∈ P} (verified with pp.explicit: Set.smulSet ∘ Set.smulSet over Equiv.Perm.applyMulAction). c05/c06/c01 are essentially equivalent; c04 (Setoid + let-bindings inside the theorem) and c08 (inlined conditions, Ω as an outer theorem variable, ncard) are correct but less idiomatic. Final file = c07's definitions, API lemma, rfl test and theorem, plus c05's non-vacuity test exhibiting a 2-section of ℕ (shows k-sections exist, so 'for all P Q ∃ g' is genuinely 'single orbit'). Compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.41

by P. M. Neumann

Let $\Omega$ be a countably infinite set. For $k \geq 2$ define a *$k$-section* of
$\Omega$ to be a partition of $\Omega$ as union of $k$ infinite sets.

b) Does there exist a group that is transitive on $k$-sections but not on
$(k + 1)$-sections?

Here a "group" is a permutation group $G \leq \mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$, acting on the set of
$k$-sections by moving the blocks of a partition: $g \cdot \{A_1, \ldots, A_k\} =
\{g(A_1), \ldots, g(A_k)\}$. "Transitive on $k$-sections" means that this induced action
on the set of all $k$-sections has a single orbit.

Part c) of the problem (a proper transitive subgroup of $\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$ transitive
on $\aleph_0$-sections) has a positive answer consistent with ZFC
(S. M. Corson, S. Shelah, [arXiv:2503.12997](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12997)) and is
not formalised here.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 9.41
- [S. M. Corson, S. Shelah, *A permutation group acting transitively on certain
  collections of models*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12997)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«9.41»

variable {Ω : Type*}

/-- A `k`-section of `Ω`: a partition of `Ω` into exactly `k` infinite sets. A partition is
recorded as the (unordered) set `P` of its blocks; `P.encard = k` forces `P` to be finite
with exactly `k` blocks. -/
def IsSection (k : ℕ) (P : Set (Set Ω)) : Prop :=
  Setoid.IsPartition P ∧ (∀ A ∈ P, A.Infinite) ∧ P.encard = k

/-- A permutation group `G ≤ Sym(Ω)` is transitive on `k`-sections if for any two
`k`-sections `P` and `Q` there is some `g ∈ G` carrying `P` to `Q`. Here `g • P` is the
pointwise action `{g '' A | A ∈ P}` of `g` on the set of blocks of `P`. -/
def IsTransitiveOnSections (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ P Q : Set (Set Ω), IsSection k P → IsSection k Q → ∃ g ∈ G, g • P = Q

/-- The action of a permutation on a set of blocks moves each block by the permutation. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem smul_set_set_eq (g : Equiv.Perm Ω) (P : Set (Set Ω)) :
    g • P = (fun A : Set Ω => g '' A) '' P := by
  rfl

/-- A `k`-section has finitely many blocks. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsSection.finite {k : ℕ} {P : Set (Set Ω)} (hP : IsSection k P) : P.Finite :=
  Set.encard_ne_top_iff.mp (hP.2.2 ▸ ENat.coe_ne_top k)

/-- The even and odd natural numbers form a `2`-section of `ℕ`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isSection_even_odd : IsSection 2 {{n : ℕ | Even n}, {n : ℕ | Odd n}} := by
  have hne : {n : ℕ | Even n} ≠ {n : ℕ | Odd n} := by
    intro h
    have : (0 : ℕ) ∈ {n : ℕ | Odd n} := h ▸ Even.zero
    simp at this
  refine ⟨⟨?_, fun a => ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, not_or]
    constructor
    · intro h
      have : (0 : ℕ) ∈ {n : ℕ | Even n} := Even.zero
      simp [← h] at this
    · intro h
      have : (1 : ℕ) ∈ {n : ℕ | Odd n} := odd_one
      simp [← h] at this
  · rcases Nat.even_or_odd a with ha | ha
    · refine ⟨{n : ℕ | Even n}, ⟨by simp, ha⟩, ?_⟩
      rintro b ⟨hb, hab⟩
      simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hb
      rcases hb with rfl | rfl
      · rfl
      · exact absurd ha (Nat.not_even_iff_odd.mpr hab)
    · refine ⟨{n : ℕ | Odd n}, ⟨by simp, ha⟩, ?_⟩
      rintro b ⟨hb, hab⟩
      simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hb
      rcases hb with rfl | rfl
      · exact absurd ha (Nat.not_odd_iff_even.mpr hab)
      · rfl
  · simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq_or_imp, forall_eq]
    constructor
    · exact Set.infinite_of_not_bddAbove fun ⟨M, hM⟩ =>
        absurd (hM (show Even (2 * (M + 1)) from even_two_mul _)) (by omega)
    · exact Set.infinite_of_not_bddAbove fun ⟨M, hM⟩ =>
        absurd (hM (show Odd (2 * M + 1) from odd_two_mul_add_one _)) (by omega)
  · rw [Set.encard_pair hne]
    rfl

/--
Let $\Omega$ be a countably infinite set. For $k \geq 2$ define a $k$-section of $\Omega$
to be a partition of $\Omega$ as union of $k$ infinite sets. Does there exist a group
$G \leq \mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$ that is transitive on $k$-sections but not on
$(k + 1)$-sections?

The question is read as asking, for every $k \geq 2$, whether such a group $G$ (depending
on $k$) exists; the same $G$ is required to be transitive on $k$-sections and not
transitive on $(k+1)$-sections.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.41».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (Ω : Type) [Countable Ω] [Infinite Ω] (k : ℕ), 2 ≤ k →
      ∃ G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω),
        IsTransitiveOnSections G k ∧ ¬ IsTransitiveOnSections G (k + 1) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.41»

items: Quantifier on k read as 'for every k ≥ 2 there exists G (depending on k)', as fixed by the decomposition table; the alternative reading '∃ k ≥ 2 ∃ G' was not used.

Ω is quantified universally over all countably infinite types (`[Countable Ω] [Infinite Ω]`) inside the statement rather than fixed to ℕ; the two are equivalent since all conditions transfer along bijections.

A k-section is an unordered partition (a `Set (Set Ω)` of blocks), not an ordered k-tuple of blocks; transitivity on ordered tuples would be a strictly stronger condition and is not what the notebook's 'partition of Ω as union of k infinite sets' describes.

'Group' is interpreted as an arbitrary subgroup of `Equiv.Perm Ω` (no transitivity on Ω or properness required), per the table's notes for part b) — the extra hypotheses 'transitive permutation group' and 'proper subgroup' appear only in part c).
The action `g • P` is Mathlib's scoped `Pointwise` instance `Set.mulActionSet` applied twice; the test lemma `smul_set_set_eq` (proved by `rfl`) pins it down as `{g '' A | A ∈ P}`.
Block count expressed with `Set.encard = k` (exact, forces finiteness) rather than `ncard`/`Nat.card`, which return 0 on infinite sets.

reviewer_notes: Interpretive points: (1) The quantifier on k is implicit in the notebook; following the decomposition table it is read as 'for every k ≥ 2, does there exist such a G (depending on k)'. An alternative reading '∃ k ≥ 2 ∃ G' exists but was not used; the docstring records the chosen reading. (2) 'Group' is any subgroup of Sym(Ω) (no transitivity on Ω, no properness) — those hypotheses appear only in part c). (3) k-sections are unordered (sets of blocks), consistent with 'partition as union of k infinite sets' and with Corson–Shelah's explicit caveat that sections are identified up to relabelling of blocks. (4) Ω is universally quantified over all countably infinite types inside the statement; this is equivalent to fixing Ω = ℕ since everything transports along bijections, and keeps all quantifiers after answer(sorry). Boundary cases: k ≥ 2 so IsSection is never used at k = 0 (where encard = 0 would only be satisfied by the empty family, which is not a partition of nonempty Ω anyway); countably infinite Ω has k-sections for every k ≥ 2, so 'transitive' is not vacuous. Part c) was dropped by the table; c01 objected that it is statable in ZFC (∃ proper transitive G transitive on ℵ₀-sections), which is a reasonable objection — its ZFC status is open (Corson–Shelah only give consistency under MA(σ-centered)) — but per the task instructions it was not formalized. answer(True) asserts a positive answer for every k ≥ 2; answer(False) asserts that for some k ≥ 2 (and some countably infinite Ω) no such group exists.
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a countably infinite set. For $k
\geq 2$ define a $k$-section of $\Omega$ to be a partition of $\Omega$ as union of $k$ infinite sets.

b) Does there exist a group that is transitive on $k$-sections but not on $(k + 1)$-sections?

*c) Does there exist a transitive permutation group on $\Omega$ that is transitive on $\aleph _0$-sections but which is a proper subgroup of ${\rm Sym}(\Omega )$?

statement_tex:
Let $\Omega$ be a countably infinite set. For $k
\geq 2$ define a {\it $k$-section\/} of $\Omega$ to be a partition
of $\Omega$ as union of $k$ infinite sets.

\makebox[25pt][r]{b)} Does there exist a group that is
transitive on
$k$-sections
but not on $(k + 1)$-sections?

\makebox[25pt][r]{\zv c)}
Does there exist a transitive permutation
group on $\Omega$ that is transitive on $\aleph _0$-sections but
which is a proper subgroup of ${\rm Sym}(\Omega )$?
title: Conjecture 9.41
